skill.name: skill-check
skill.description: Tests and validates Agent Skills for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Use it to run quick, standard, or deep checks on an existing skill directory, including structure, security, evals, scripts, and output quality.
skill.summary: Validates existing Agent Skills with structured checks for quality, security, evals, scripts, and outputs.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, validation documentation, and deliberate eval fixtures. I found two semantic risks: execution of target skill scripts during Standard or Deep checks, and package installation guidance that can alter system Python. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Standard and Deep checks execute scripts from the target skill.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before all script execution, recommend sandboxing, and default unknown community skills to Quick Check.

remediation.issue: Mock generation guidance uses pip install with --break-system-packages.
remediation.suggestion: Replace these commands with virtual environment guidance, dependency preflight checks, or user-approved project-local installs.

remediation.issue: Skill discovery can search common personal and private skill locations.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for a path first and confirm before searching broad user skill directories or MCP filesystem roots.

semantic_findings.title: Target Skill Script Execution During Standard Checks
semantic_findings.description: Standard and Deep workflows include executing scripts from the skill being tested. This can run untrusted community code if the user selects an unsafe target skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly include script execution with mock inputs and sample commands. Existing warnings reduce risk, but execution remains part of the default Standard path.

semantic_findings.title: System Python Package Installation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The mock file guidance tells agents to install packages with --break-system-packages. That can modify the host Python environment and bypass package manager safeguards.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicit pip install examples using --break-system-packages. The packages are common, but the installation method is risky for shared environments.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need evidence that a skill works and does not expose users to avoidable risk. SkillCheck reviews structure, security, evals, scripts, and outputs through tiered checks.
actual_capabilities: Runs Quick, Standard, and Deep validation workflows for existing skill directories.
Checks SKILL.md frontmatter, references, assets, paths, dependencies, and cross-file consistency.
Compares documented script invocations with actual script arguments and outputs.
Reviews skill scripts and instructions for dangerous security patterns.
Processes evals/evals.json cases and records pass or fail evidence.
Generates mock inputs for common text, document, image, archive, and code file types.
limitations: Standard and Deep checks may execute target skill scripts, so unsafe skills need sandboxing.
Binary mock generation may require optional Python packages that are not installed.
Static review can miss novel vulnerabilities or context-specific misuse.
It reports findings for existing skills and does not create or edit skills.

use_cases.title: Pre-release skill validation
use_cases.description: Run a structured check before publishing a new skill to users or a marketplace.

use_cases.title: Regression testing after changes
use_cases.description: Re-run evals, script tests, and output checks after updating a skill.

use_cases.title: Security-focused marketplace review
use_cases.description: Inspect scripts, file access, instructions, and execution risks before accepting a community skill.

prompt_templates.title: Quick structure check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation before sharing a skill.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Quick Check on the skill at ./my-skill. Report structural, security, and best practice issues.

prompt_templates.title: Standard functional check
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine validation for a skill with scripts or evals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Standard Check on the skill at ./my-skill. Include eval regression, script checks, and I/O contract validation.

prompt_templates.title: Security review only
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review before executing any target skill code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the skill at ./my-skill for instruction security and script risks. Ask before running any code that is flagged.

prompt_templates.title: Deep release gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Deep Check on ./my-skill. Include edge cases, workflow simulation, eval regression, and prioritized remediation.

output_examples.input: Quick Check the chart skill before I share it.
output_examples.output: A concise report with a verdict, passed checks, failed checks, security findings, and prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Run a Standard Check on a skill that converts CSV files to reports.
output_examples.output: A validation report covering eval results, script execution status, mock input files, output format checks, and warnings.

output_examples.input: Review this community skill for marketplace safety.
output_examples.output: A security-focused assessment that separates confirmed risks, false positives, execution concerns, and required remediation.

best_practices: Start with Quick Check for unknown skills, then decide whether execution-based tests are safe.
Review the test plan before Standard or Deep checks run target skill scripts.
Use an isolated workspace for mock files, generated outputs, and captured test evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not run target scripts after critical security findings without explicit user approval.
Do not treat the best practice score as the same thing as the functional verdict.
Do not skip discovery and read only SKILL.md when a skill has supporting files.

faq.question: Does SkillCheck create or modify skills?
faq.answer: No. It tests existing skills and reports findings, recommendations, and evidence.

faq.question: What is the default check depth?
faq.answer: Standard is the default. It includes static checks, eval regression, script tests, and basic output validation.

faq.question: Can it run without executing target scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Quick Check for static structure, security, and best practice review only.

faq.question: How does it handle dangerous scripts?
faq.answer: It runs security review first and instructs the agent to warn before executing scripts with critical findings.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is declared for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible environments.

faq.question: What evidence does a report include?
faq.answer: Reports include test IDs, pass or fail status, observed behavior, affected files, and suggested fixes.
